maria (docs): FYI I opened a PR to consolidate retention guidance, add a migration checklist, and include SDK snippets across languages. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5450 :wave:

derek (security): Thanks. Please include: (1) short vs medium vs long example TTLs, (2) both pseudonymization and redaction examples, and (3) a clear line that hashing alone is NOT sufficient for high-risk identifiers.

ana (legal): small correction: call the customer-facing line a "summary"; keep the detailed playbook internal. I'll draft the legal-hold wording and an exception request flow.

harper (eng-docs): I'll add Go and Java snippets (some teams use JVM infra). Question: show KMS salt usage inline or reference our crypto helper?

derek (security): Show a short KMS example in Go for clarity, but recommend calling the vetted helper in production. Also add deterministic vs nondeterministic note.

maria (docs): Proposed example TTLs: 30 days (short), 180 days (medium), 5 years (long). Mark as "illustrative only - consult legal/security".

harper (eng-docs): Go snippet (illustrative):
```go
// illustrative: use vetted crypto helper in prod
package pseudonymize
import ("crypto/hmac" "crypto/sha256")
func Pseudo(id string, salt []byte) string {
    mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, salt)
    mac.Write([]byte(id))
    sum := mac.Sum(nil)
    return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum)[:24]
}
```

derek (security): Add a short paragraph about re-identification risk: salted deterministic pseudonyms can be necessary for analytics but increase risk; nondeterministic tokens (rotateable) are safer for deletion flows.
